caseno: Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 91 of 2001.
lawyer:
Sharifuddin Chaklader, Advocate-on-Record —For the Petitioners 
Not represented— State Respondent.
parties:
Towled Hossain (Md) and others ------ Petitioners
Vs.
State ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
Abu Sayeed Ahammed J: The accused petitioners seek leave to appeal against the judgment and order dated 26-6-2000 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division, discharging the Rule obtained in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 127 of 1995 and consequent thereupon affirming the judgment and order dated 16-11-1994 passed by the Additional Sessions Judge, Narayanganj, in Criminal Revision No. 27 of 1991, affirming the order dated 6-10-1990 passed by the Upazila Magistrate in GR Case No. 454 of 1987 arising out of Narayanganj PS Case No. 5(12)87 under section 16(ka) and 25 of the Special Powers Act. 

 2. Khandaker Fazle Rahim, Inspector of Police, CID Bangladesh, at that time of Munshiganj Camp, lodged an FIR with Narayanganj Police Station registered as Narayanganj PS case No. 5(12) 87 dated 10-12-1987. The police started investigation in the case. But could not complete the investigation within the stipulated period as required under section 167 of the Code of Criminal Procedure as amended and, as such, the Upazila Magistrate where the case was pending, extended time for 30 days on 5-6-1988 to complete the investigation. Later on, further time for 60 days and then again 45 days was extended for completing the investigation, by the Sessions Judge Narayanganj in Miscellaneous Case No. 677 of 1988. Since the investigation could not be completed by the extended time the Upazila Magistrate by order dated 18-12-1988 stopped the investigation of the case and released the petitioner. But later on, by order dated 16-9-1990 contained in memo No. 363 (ka) of the Additional District Magistrate, Narayanganj vis-a-vis the Government, revived the case and the Upazila Magistrate by his order dated 6-10-1990 accepted the police report No. 190 dated 13-9-1990 submitted by the police after completing the investigation. 

 3. Against the said order of revival of the case petitioners preferred Criminal Revision No. 27 of 1991 before the Sessions Judge, Narayanganj and the Sessions Judge upon hearing both sides rejected the revisional application by order dated 16-11-1994 finding that there was no illegality in reviving the case by the Government. 

 4. The petitioner thereafter moved before the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 127 of 1995 and obtained the Rule. 

 5. The High Court Division, after proper consideration of the case and materials on record found that the Magistrate, in a case being triable under Special Powers Act, had no legal jurisdiction to release the accused person and he is required simply to transmit the records of the case to the Senior Special Judge, namely, the Sessions Judge, for necessary order and therefore, the High Court Division rightly held that the order releasing the accused petitioner passed by the Upazila Magistrate was without jurisdiction and rightly affirmed the decision of the Sessions Judge by rejecting the revisional application of the accused person. Against the aforesaid order of the High Court Division this leave petition has been filed. 

 6. On behalf of the accused petitioner, the argument has been advanced that the order of revival of the case, after expiry of the stipulated period as provided by law, namely, section 167 of the Code of Criminal. Procedure, as amended, is illegal and the High Court Division committed illegality in discharging the Rule. The High Court Division, as it is noticed, has correctly found that the revival order was not in any manner illegal and the same was passed by the government in accordance with law. 

 7. Mr. Sharifuddin Chaklader, the learned Advocate-on-record, submits that the revival order was not a legal order but he could not support the ground of the petitioner that they were released legally by the Upazila Magistrate and Mr. Chaklader could not deny that the Upazila Magistrate had any legal authority to release the accused persons in a case under section 16(A) and 25 of the Special Powers Act during the investigation stage and in such a case the Special Tribunal or a Magistrate should have sent the case records to the Senior Special Judge who is the Sessions Judge as well for holding trial of the case by the appropriate Court.
